name: version-command
body: kalide exposes its build-stamped version to users: `kalide version` (and `--version`/`-v` accepted as a top-level flag equivalent) prints the version string stamped at build time via `-ldflags -X main.version=...` (`dev` for unbuilt/source runs) to stdout and exits 0. Output format: a single line `kalide <version>` (e.g. `kalide v0.5.0`, `kalide dev`). This reverses the prior "no user-facing surface" design for the `version` variable in `cmd/kalide/main.go` — see requirements.note.reconcile-version-surface — while leaving the build-time stamping mechanism itself unchanged. AC: `kalide version`, `kalide --version` and `kalide -v` each print exactly one line `kalide <version>` to stdout and exit 0; a release binary built with `-ldflags "-X main.version=vX.Y.Z"` prints `kalide vX.Y.Z`; an unstamped build prints `kalide dev`.
